name: commit-list
title: Commit list
description: Commits grouped by day under sticky headings: subject link, author, time in words, CI status as a glyph and word, and a short hash that copies.
docs: commits is { hash, message, body?, author: { name, image? }, committedAt, status?, merge?, href? }[], newest first, and they are grouped by calendar day in timeZone (default UTC) under headings that stick while their commits scroll past; set --commit-list-top on the list to park them under a fixed header. The first line of message is the subject: with href it is a link, without one but with onSelect a button. onSelect(commit, event) runs on both, so a client-side router can call event.preventDefault(). Whatever follows the first line of message (or body) folds behind a disclosure button. status is success, failure, running, pending or cancelled and is always a glyph plus a word (labels.statuses to translate). The short hash copies the full hash. Times are words (3 minutes ago, yesterday) with the exact moment in a tooltip that a tap opens too; pass now to pin the clock for server HTML and tests, otherwise the list reads the browser clock after the first paint and writes the full date until then. The row lays itself out by the width of the list, not of the window, so it also works in a narrow column.
